finding.claim: Unrestricted SSRF in /preview: the user-supplied url query parameter is passed directly to requests.get with no host, IP, or scheme validation, and the first 500 characters of the response body are returned to the caller.
finding.source: Query parameter 'url' via request.args.get at app.py:15

trace.note: target = request.args.get('url', '') takes attacker-controlled input from the query string
requests.get(target, timeout=5) issues the outbound request to the attacker-chosen URL
Returns resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] to the caller, so response contents are readable (full-read SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. No hostname, IP range, or scheme check, and no authentication on the route. requests only permits http/https, so file:// is rejected by the library; this was reasoned from library behaviour and not executed.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /preview handler (app.py:13-17) has no hostname, IP, or scheme check and no authentication. The only allowlist, ALLOWED_HOSTS at app.py:9 with the check at app.py:23-25, is in the separate /partner route and does not cover /preview.
verdict.reason: At app.py:15 the value comes straight from request.args.get("url") on an unauthenticated route, it is passed to requests.get at app.py:16 with no validation, and app.py:17 returns resp.text[:500] to the caller, so the SSRF is real and readable.

finding.claim: SSRF via redirect in /partner: the hostname allowlist is applied only to the initial URL, and requests.get follows redirects by default, so an allowlisted partner host can redirect the server to an internal address. Only the status code is returned, making this closer to blind SSRF.
finding.source: Query parameter 'url' via request.args.get at app.py:22

trace.note: host = urlparse(target).hostname extracts the hostname for the check
if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS returns 400, so only api.partner.example and cdn.partner.example pass the initial check
requests.get(target, timeout=5) follows 3xx redirects by default, so an allowlisted host can redirect to an internal or metadata address
Returns only resp.status_code, so the response body is not exposed

finding.guards_checked: Exact hostname match against ALLOWED_HOSTS at app.py:23-24, applied to the initial URL only. No redirect handling, no allow_redirects=False, no resolved-IP check. Exploitation requires an allowlisted partner host that redirects, or one that is compromised.

verdict.guard_found: app.py:23-24: parsed-hostname exact set membership (`urlparse(target).hostname not in ALLOWED_HOSTS` → 400). This is the closing guard form the rubric lists. It applies to the initial URL only; app.py:26 `requests.get(target, timeout=5)` has no `allow_redirects=False` and no redirect-target check.
verdict.reason: Under the verification rules, the exact hostname set check at app.py:23-24 is a closing guard, so the finding is refuted, even though the candidate's trace is accurate (app.py:22, 23, 24, 26, 27 all match the description) and the query-parameter source at app.py:22 is attacker-controlled. The redirect gap the candidate describes is real and unaddressed by that guard (app.py:26 follows 3xx by default), so this should be fixed by passing allow_redirects=False or re-validating each redirect hop, and the rule's guard-form test may be worth revisiting for cases like this where the check covers only the first hop.
